intro.greeting: Hello Friends and Members of Chorlton Bikes,
paragraphs: We're really glad you're here. This newsletter is a chance to share what we've been up to - our riders, our partners, and the difference we're making together in Chorlton and beyond.
August has been a month of community celebrations, new kit on the way and plenty of trishaw smiles across Greater Manchester. Here's what we've been up to.

monthIntro: From a new family cargo bike and Pride parade rides to summer fun days, festival leaflets and plans for our second Community Ride, August has been full of zero-emissions momentum.

sections.title: Our new family cargo bike is on its way!
bullets: 🚚 Thanks to funding from TfGM, we've ordered an Estarli Longtail electric cargo bike, capable of carrying up to three children, with a maximum combined weight of 110kg.
🚚 And the best bit? It will be completely free to hire for one week!

🚚 We want to give local families the chance to try out an electric cargo bike and discover how it could make everyday journeys easier, cheaper and more fun - less time stuck in traffic jams and more time enjoying the journey!

cta.label: Register your interest in hiring the family cargo bike

images.alt: Estarli Longtail electric cargo bike for Chorlton Bikes bike library

sections.title: The Community will ride!
bullets: 🚴 Thanks to the Your Neighbourhood Fund, we will hold our 2nd Annual Community Ride at some point in late September/early October.
🚴 We've also secured the services of Luke Shepherd to document the event with another of his amazing films.

🚴 We're waiting for the installation of Bailey Bridge, which was delayed to late September. Once we hear definitive news about the bridge, we'll promote the ride on a centrally located banner, posters in key locations and on social media.
🚴 As always, nothing can rival the power of word of mouth - so when we have secured a date, we'll tell you... and you can tell everyone!

sections.title: Belvoir Green Community Fun Day
bullets: 🌿 Tom piloted the trishaw for Belvoir Green's community fun day on 10th August.
🌿 It was a day organised by Taskforce, Friends of the Earth, Keep Manchester Tidy, Noor Masjid Mosque and Manchester City Council.
🌿 It was great to see so many parts of the community in Levenshulme coming together and having a go on the trishaw!

images.alt: Trishaw at Belvoir Green Community Fun Day

sections.title: Trishaws at Ride and Stride, and Family Fun Days
bullets: 🚲 The trishaw has been a real vehicle for joy and celebration at several community events this summer!
🚲 Chris took the trishaw for a spin at the Ride and Stride Festival at Seymour Park on 12th August, giving people the chance to experience the joy of cycling together.
🚲 Tom brought the trishaw along to Merseybank Family Fun Day, giving rides to local residents and helping bring plenty of smiles to the day.
🚲 And finally, Glynis spent the day at Old Moat Family Fun Day, taking lots of happy locals out for a spin.
🚲 It's fantastic to see the trishaw becoming part of so many local events and helping people of all ages get out, connect with their community and enjoy the simple pleasure of a bike ride.

sections.title: Bye Scarlett!
bullets: 💚 We said goodbye to our rider Scarlett, who has been riding with us since 2024.
💚 She's finished her degree and is moving out of the area.
💚 Scarlett has been an invaluable rider for us, doing collections and deliveries for the NHS, catering jobs and surplus for food banks.
💚 We will miss her and wish her all the best for the future!

sections.title: Leaflets delivered for Live at Wythenshawe
bullets: 🎵 Albert has delivered leaflets to Wythenshawe residents for us for the last couple of years for the Live @ Wythenshawe music festival.
🎵 He is always super reliable and flexible when a few extra leaflets need to be delivered.
🎵 We're grateful that Live @ Wythenshawe continues to choose us to deliver the letters and permits for this local live music event, which continues to grow and gain success each year.
🎵 Albert earned a spot on the guest list for seeing Pulp play as a thank you from the company!

images.alt: Live at Wythenshawe music festival leaflet delivery

sections.title: RHS Cycle Hire Scheme
bullets: 🚲 On 6th August, Manchester Bikes invited Chorlton Bikes along for the launch of the RHS Bridgewater Bike Hire Scheme.
🚲 Reg attended with Salford City Council and other cycling active travel dignitaries.
🚲 The service is operated by Manchester Bikes. To access the bikes, users must download and use the dedicated community bikeshare app developed by MOSA.
🚲 The bikes are free to hire and users get 30% off the entrance fee.

images.alt: Reg at the RHS Bridgewater Bike Hire Scheme launch

sections.title: Manchester Climate Ready
bullets: 🌍 After meeting Ellie Bradley from Manchester Climate Ready, we should soon find out if our application to be a member has been ratified by their board.
🌍 We will be able to link up with other organisations across Manchester who have signed up to their mission to make Manchester a zero-carbon, climate-resilient city.
🌍 We will also be able to shine a light on our work and encourage other partners to use bike deliveries in the city.

sections.title: Trishaw takes on Pride!
bullets: 🏳️‍🌈 Our volunteer and founder, Glynis, had the pleasure of taking Cllr Tracey Rawlins - Disability Advocate for the Bee Network and Deputy Leader of Manchester City Council - out on the trishaw for the Pride parade!
🏳️‍🌈 Despite the rather terrible weather, they had a fantastic time celebrating Pride together.
🏳️‍🌈 We love seeing the trishaw bringing people together and helping make Manchester's events more accessible for everyone.

paragraphs: Thank you to everyone for the continued energy, care and commitment that keeps Chorlton Bikes moving forward - especially our riders and volunteers who brought the trishaw to so many summer events.

Whether you're riding, volunteering, donating, or simply spreading the word, you're helping us build a stronger and more connected community. Here's to the Community Ride ahead - and watch this space for a date! 🚲💚
